activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Identifying the pronunciation of various sounds in syllables, words, sentences and texts
activities.learning_activity: (a) Pronouncing consonant cluster sounds ngw, ndw, njw, mbw and nzw
suggested_methods: Demonstration: Guide pupils to pronounce the consonant cluster sounds ngw, ndw, njw, mbw and nzw by imitating your pronunciation, or show pupils a video on the pronunciation of the mentioned consonant cluster sounds and then guide them to pronounce the sounds
Question and answer: Guide pupils to ask and answer questions that have answers containing the consonant cluster sounds ngw, ndw, njw, mbw and nzw
Text analysis: Guide pupils to read texts containing the consonant cluster sounds ngw, ndw, njw, mbw and nzw, and then identify those letters
Game: Use word cards/floor drawing blocks to guide pupils to pronounce the consonant cluster sounds ngw, ndw, njw, mbw and nzw. For each block, write one consonant cluster
activities.assessment_criteria: The consonant cluster sounds ngw, ndw, njw, mbw and nzw are pronounced correctly
suggested_resources: texts with story passages containing the consonant cluster sounds ngw, ndw, njw, mbw and nzw

activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Identifying the pronunciation of various sounds in syllables, words, sentences and texts
activities.learning_activity: (b) Pronouncing consonant cluster sounds in syllables, words, sentences and texts
suggested_methods: Role play: Guide pupils to role-play the performance of various activities, in which they will use consonant cluster sounds
Tongue twister: Guide pupils to read sentences with words containing consecutive consonant cluster sounds
activities.assessment_criteria: The consonant cluster sounds in syllables, words, sentences and texts are pronounced correctly

activities.learning_activity: (a) Using vocabulary related to daily life to initiate and develop conversations with confidence in various contexts
suggested_methods: Role play: Guide pupils to role-play daily activities in different contexts using appropriate vocabulary and with confidence
Word game: Guide pupils to form words starting with each letter of a word related to daily life
activities.assessment_criteria: Vocabulary related to daily life has been used to initiate and develop conversations in various contexts with confidence

activities.learning_activity: (b) Identifying synonyms and antonyms in conversations
suggested_methods: Story: Guide pupils to identify synonyms and antonyms from the conversation
Field trip: Guide pupils to make a field trip to identify the names of objects with synonyms and antonyms, and then present
activities.assessment_criteria: Synonyms and antonyms are identified correctly in conversations

activities.learning_activity: (c) Describing objects found in the environment in singular and plural forms
suggested_methods: Observation: Guide pupils to observe objects in their environment, and then identify the singular and plural forms of those objects
Demonstration: Guide pupils to identify the singular and plural forms of various objects that you will show them
activities.assessment_criteria: Objects found in the environment have been described correctly in singular and plural forms

activities.learning_activity: (d) Asking and answering questions
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide pupils to discuss any given topic, and then ask each other questions
Chain: Guide pupils to ask each other questions and answer in a chain sequence
activities.assessment_criteria: Questions are asked and answered fluently

activities.learning_activity: (e) Changing intonation according to emotions or the context of the conversation
suggested_methods: Narration: Guide pupils to narrate various events in order to change intonation and express different emotions
activities.assessment_criteria: Intonation has been changed correctly according to emotions or the context of the conversation

activities.learning_activity: (f) Initiating and completing riddles, proverbs and idioms in conversations
suggested_methods: Observation: Guide pupils using pictures/real objects to pose and solve riddles, initiate and complete proverbs, and explain the meanings of idioms and proverbs
Game: Guide pupils in two teams to pose and solve riddles, initiate and complete proverbs, and explain the meanings of idioms
activities.assessment_criteria: Riddles, proverbs and idioms are initiated and completed correctly in conversations

activities.specific_competence: 1.3 Using writing in communication according to various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (a) Writing a passage using punctuation marks: full stop (.), exclamation mark (!), question mark (?) and comma (,)
suggested_methods: Dictation: Read to pupils a prepared passage and have them write it using punctuation marks: full stop (.), exclamation mark (!), question mark (?) and comma (,)
activities.assessment_criteria: A passage is written using punctuation marks correctly: full stop (.), exclamation mark (!), question mark (?) and comma (,)

activities.specific_competence: 1.3 Using writing in communication according to various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (b) Writing a passage using cohesive conjunctions
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide pupils to read texts, and then identify and discuss words that serve to show connection or linkage between sentences or word phrases (phrase and phrase)
activities.assessment_criteria: A passage is written using cohesive conjunctions

activities.specific_competence: 1.3 Using writing in communication according to various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (c) Using punctuation marks correctly when writing dictation
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide pupils to discuss the importance and correct use of punctuation marks, and then write dictation observing those marks
Narration: Guide pupils to listen to recorded narratives, and then write what they heard while observing punctuation marks
activities.assessment_criteria: Punctuation marks are used correctly when writing dictation

activities.specific_competence: 1.3 Using writing in communication according to various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (d) Using prepositions (behind, in front of, on top of, beside, under, in the middle of and around/next to) in writing
suggested_methods: Demonstration: Show pupils real objects or pictures you have prepared, and then guide them to identify where objects are located based on the identified prepositions
activities.assessment_criteria: Prepositions (behind, in front of, on top of, beside, under, in the middle of and around/next to) are used correctly in writing

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of something listened to or read
activities.learning_activity: (a) Listening to conversations while focusing on key matters in various contexts
suggested_methods: Narration: Guide pupils to narrate stories or news to each other, and then answer questions while focusing on key matters in various contexts
activities.assessment_criteria: Conversations focusing on key matters in various contexts have been listened to

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of something listened to or read
activities.learning_activity: (b) Using words heard in other conversational contexts
suggested_methods: Demonstration: Show pupils pictures or real objects, and then guide them to use words corresponding to those objects according to context
activities.assessment_criteria: Words heard in other conversational contexts are used correctly

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of something listened to or read
activities.learning_activity: (c) Using a dictionary to find the meanings of new vocabulary appearing in short simple texts
suggested_methods: Story: Prepare a story showing the function of a dictionary
Project work: Give pupils several words from a short simple text, and then have them look up definitions in the dictionary
activities.assessment_criteria: A dictionary is used to find the meanings of new vocabulary appearing in short simple texts

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of something listened to or read
activities.learning_activity: (d) Answering text-based questions correctly
suggested_methods: Media: Guide pupils to listen to information in a text, and then ask questions regarding that text
Discussion: Guide pupils to discuss the importance of education using a text, and then ask questions
activities.assessment_criteria: Text-based questions are answered correctly

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of something listened to or read
activities.specific_competence: 2.2 Reading texts fluently and with comprehension
activities.learning_activity: (a) Reading short and simple texts at an appropriate speed and with correct pronunciation
suggested_methods: Demonstration: Read a short and simple text at an appropriate speed according to the age of your pupils, with correct pronunciation, intonation and punctuation marks as an example, and then guide them to read
activities.assessment_criteria: Short and simple texts are read at an appropriate speed and with correct pronunciation

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of something listened to or read
activities.specific_competence: 2.2 Reading texts fluently and with comprehension
activities.learning_activity: (b) Reading sentences observing the rising and falling of sound waves
suggested_methods: Observation: Guide pupils to identify sentences with different pitch levels using ICT equipment, and then guide them to repeat pronouncing those sentences to show different intonations
Question and Answer: Guide pupils to construct sentences, and then read them aloud observing the rising and falling of sound waves
activities.assessment_criteria: Sentences are read fluently while observing the rising and falling of sound waves

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of something listened to or read
activities.specific_competence: 2.2 Reading texts fluently and with comprehension
activities.learning_activity: (c) Explaining the main message contained in a short text read
suggested_methods: Question and answer: Guide pupils to read a short text, and then ask questions about the main message from the text
activities.assessment_criteria: The main message contained in the short text read is explained fluently

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and writing according to context
activities.learning_activity: (a) Writing various sentences correctly
suggested_methods: Game: Prepare sentences, then cut those sentences into words and mix up the word cards. Guide pupils to form sentences and write them using the words written on the cards
activities.assessment_criteria: Various sentences are written correctly

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and writing according to context
activities.learning_activity: (b) Arranging mixed sentences in a correct sequence
suggested_methods: Question and answer: Prepare sentences with incorrect word order, and then guide pupils to write those sentences correctly

Field trip: Guide pupils to visit a neighboring school, and then narrate their field trip step by step. Write those steps using complete sentences, then mix up the sentences and ask pupils to arrange them in logical order
activities.assessment_criteria: Mixed sentences are arranged in a correct sequence

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and writing according to context
activities.learning_activity: (c) Writing a short text observing proper word arrangement and punctuation marks
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide pupils to discuss the proper arrangement of words and the importance of punctuation marks in writing a short text, and then write a short text observing these aspects
activities.assessment_criteria: A short text is written correctly observing proper word arrangement and punctuation marks

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.2 Analyzing ideas presented in various texts
activities.learning_activity: (a) Identifying vocabulary appearing in short simple texts
suggested_methods: Project work: Guide pupils to read short simple texts and listen to news on television, radio or phone, and then identify the vocabulary contained along with their definitions
Story: Guide pupils to read or listen to a story, and then name new words and look up their meanings in a dictionary
activities.assessment_criteria: Vocabulary appearing in short simple texts has been identified

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.2 Analyzing ideas presented in various texts
activities.learning_activity: (b) Analyzing main ideas emerging in short simple texts
suggested_methods: Jigsaw: Divide different texts among groups, guide pupils to read and write the message of those texts, and then ensure each group reads all the work and explains key issues contained in the respective text
activities.assessment_criteria: Main ideas emerging in short simple texts have been analyzed effectively

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.3 Demonstrating early skills in creating various Kiswahili works
activities.learning_activity: (a) Narrating short simple stories
suggested_methods: Narration: Guide pupils to tell stories to each other, then select a few pupils to narrate their stories in front of the class
activities.assessment_criteria: Short simple stories are narrated correctly

activities.learning_activity: (a) Comparing things using words (kuliko, zaidi ya, kama, mithili ya and mfano wa) in various contexts
suggested_methods: Demonstration: Display two items at a time, then guide students to explain the concept of comparison
Question and answer: Prepare a table with comparison words, then guide students to construct sentences using the table
activities.assessment_criteria: Things are compared correctly using words (kuliko, zaidi ya, kama, mithili ya and mfano wa) in various contexts fluently

activities.learning_activity: (b) Narrating events considering tense markers: present (-na-), past (-li-), future (-ta-); and perfect aspect (-me-) and habitual aspect (hu-)
suggested_methods: Concept map: Guide students through a chart to explain types of tenses and aspects
Question and answer: Guide students to construct sentences considering tense and aspect markers
activities.assessment_criteria: Events are narrated accurately in various tenses and aspects

activities.learning_activity: (c) Expressing oneself with confidence
suggested_methods: Debate: Give students a topic and divide them into two groups, then guide them to engage in a debate with confidence
Role play: Guide students to role-play with confidence
activities.assessment_criteria: Expressing oneself with confidence is done fluently

activities.learning_activity: (d) Supporting or opposing an idea using arguments and simple examples
suggested_methods: Ngonjera (poetic dialogue): Give students a topic and roles, then guide their dialogue and summarize the raised arguments
activities.assessment_criteria: An idea is supported and opposed using arguments and simple examples

activities.learning_activity: (e) Using idioms and proverbs in conversation
suggested_methods: Pictures and descriptions: Draw pictures and put idioms and proverbs for each picture then guide students to identify the relationship of idioms, proverbs and their pictures, then use those idioms and proverbs according to their meanings
Storytelling: Guide students to create stories using idioms and proverbs
activities.assessment_criteria: Idioms and proverbs are used well in conversation

activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Using writing in communication according to various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (a) Composing simple texts using punctuation marks: hyphen (-), slash (/), brackets ( ) and quotation marks (“ ”)
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students to compose simple texts using illustrations of punctuation marks correctly
activities.assessment_criteria: Simple texts are composed correctly using punctuation marks: hyphen (-), slash (/), brackets ( ) and quotation marks (“ ”)

activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Using writing in communication according to various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (b) Using tenses and aspects correctly in writing a paragraph
suggested_methods: Reading texts: Prepare texts that use various tenses and aspects, then guide students to identify those tenses and aspects by underlining, then construct sentences using those tenses and aspects
activities.assessment_criteria: Tenses and aspects are used correctly in writing a paragraph

activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Using writing in communication according to various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (c) Writing simple texts considering a proper flow of ideas
suggested_methods: Narration: Prepare pictures that build a story, mix them up, then guide students to write a story considering the correct sequence of the given pictures
activities.assessment_criteria: A simple text is written considering the correct flow of ideas

activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Using writing in communication according to various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (d) Writing a friendly letter considering the correct structure
suggested_methods: Discussion: Distribute friendly letters into groups, then guide students to discuss their parts
Boasting game: Give students the roles of the parts of a friendly letter, then guide them to boast in front of the class according to the characteristics of those parts
activities.assessment_criteria: A friendly letter is written considering the correct structure

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of what has been listened to or read
activities.learning_activity: (a) Listening to stories
suggested_methods: Storytelling: Guide students to listen to stories on the radio/television/recorder, then ask them questions based on the story they listened to
Narration: Guide students to narrate the story they listened to
activities.assessment_criteria: The story has been listened to attentively

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of what has been listened to or read
activities.learning_activity: (b) Identifying the narrator's feelings through the rise and fall of voice tones
suggested_methods: Storytelling: Narrate a story by assuming the role of each character considering the rise and fall of voice tones, then guide students to name the characteristics of each character based on their role
activities.assessment_criteria: The narrator's feelings are identified correctly based on the rise and fall of voice tones

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of what has been listened to or read
activities.learning_activity: (c) Identifying the main message from a story listened to
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students in groups to discuss the main message from the story they listened to
activities.assessment_criteria: The main message in the listened story is identified

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of what has been listened to or read
activities.learning_activity: (a) Reading short simple texts fluently
suggested_methods: Field trip: Direct students to go to the library to read short simple texts, then return to the class and narrate the texts to each other
Reading aloud: Guide students to read short simple texts aloud considering appropriate speed, correct pronunciation and punctuation marks
activities.assessment_criteria: Short simple texts are read fluently

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of what has been listened to or read
activities.learning_activity: (b) Answering questions based on a short text read
suggested_methods: Question and answer: Guide students to answer questions related to the texts they have read
Rotational papers: Distribute different questions concerning the text, then each group writes answers on paper and passes the paper with answers to other groups to read those groups' answers
activities.assessment_criteria: Questions based on the short text read are answered correctly

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of what has been listened to or read
activities.learning_activity: (c) Using new vocabulary and expressions contained in the short text read
suggested_methods: Reading texts: Guide students to read short texts and identify new vocabulary and expressions in creative work
Question and answer: Guide students to construct stories using new vocabulary and expressions from the short texts they have read
activities.assessment_criteria: New vocabulary and expressions contained in the short text read are used correctly

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and in writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Presenting arguments through speech in various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (a) Identifying vocabulary or phrases used to build or oppose an argument (e.g., your argument is good but ..., although you are saying this, there is ...)
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students to listen to topics in media or ICT tools, then identify vocabulary or phrases used to build or oppose an argument
Debate: Guide students to build or oppose arguments using appropriate vocabulary and phrases used to build or oppose arguments
activities.assessment_criteria: Vocabulary or phrases used to build or oppose arguments are identified correctly

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and in writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Presenting arguments through speech in various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (b) Expressing opinions or ideas using vocabulary and phrases used to build or oppose arguments
suggested_methods: Debate: Guide students to build arguments or oppose arguments using appropriate vocabulary and phrases correctly
Game: Guide students to role-play that they are in a class meeting discussing how to clean the classroom using appropriate language
activities.assessment_criteria: Opinions or ideas using vocabulary and phrases used to build or oppose arguments are expressed politely

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and in writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Presenting arguments through speech in various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (c) Building arguments with logical sequence and coherence
suggested_methods: Game: Write several sentences that build a single idea (each sentence on its own paper), give students one sentence each and ensure they are mixed up, then have them arrange themselves in sequence according to the logic of the sentences
Question and answer: Guide students to match sentences in two columns
activities.assessment_criteria: Arguments are built with logical sequence and coherence

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and in writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.2 Analyzing ideas presented in various texts
activities.learning_activity: (a) Reading short simple texts
suggested_methods: Reading texts: Guide students to read short simple texts aloud and silently, then ask them questions about the text they read
Field trip: Guide students to visit a nearby library to read various texts based on the guidelines given to them, then write what they read and present it in class
activities.assessment_criteria: Short simple texts have been read

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and in writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.2 Analyzing ideas presented in various texts
activities.learning_activity: (b) Explaining the meanings of new expressions that appeared in short simple texts
suggested_methods: Reading texts: Guide students to read texts and identify vocabulary and new expressions in the texts
Project work: Guide students using dictionaries to look up the meanings of vocabulary and new expressions that appeared in the texts
Question and answer: Guide students to construct sentences using vocabulary and new expressions from the text
activities.assessment_criteria: The meanings of new expressions that appeared in texts are explained correctly

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and in writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.2 Analyzing ideas presented in various texts
activities.learning_activity: (c) Presenting main ideas contained in short simple texts
suggested_methods: Reading texts: Guide students to read short simple texts, then summarize them focusing on the main ideas contained in those texts
Game: Guide students, in two columns, through competition, to present ideas contained in the texts they read, then award marks for each idea. The column with the most marks will win
activities.assessment_criteria: Main ideas contained in short simple texts are presented correctly

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and in writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.3 Demonstrating early skills of creativity in various Kiswahili works
activities.learning_activity: (a) Composing short simple stories
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students to read short simple stories, discuss things to consider in story composition, then compose short simple stories
Narration: Guide students to narrate their lives while at school
Role play: Guide students to role-play the story they narrated about their lives while at school
activities.assessment_criteria: Short simple stories are composed well

activities.learning_activity: (a) Using vocabulary to narrate events, news, and various things with confidence
suggested_methods: Demonstration: Show students sequential pictures to narrate events, news, and various issues with confidence
activities.assessment_criteria: Vocabulary has been used in narrating events, news, and various things with confidence

activities.learning_activity: (b) Identifying grammatical persons (singular and plural) in conversations
suggested_methods: Pictures and descriptions: Show pictures that identify grammatical persons (singular and plural), meaning the three grammatical persons (singular and plural) in conversations have been identified with people engaged in various activities, then explain the three grammatical persons in their singular and plural forms

Game: Guide a game of constructing sentences by observing grammatical persons. The first column should be the first person singular and plural. Do the same for the second and third columns. Note that a single sentence will be changed across all grammatical persons
activities.assessment_criteria: The three grammatical persons (singular and plural) in conversations have been identified

activities.learning_activity: (c) Using idioms and proverbs in conversations
suggested_methods: Narration: Guide students to tell stories using idioms and proverbs correctly
activities.assessment_criteria: Idioms and proverbs have been used correctly in conversations

activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Using writing in communication according to various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (a) Writing a passage observing punctuation marks: colon (:), semicolon (;), apostrophe (‘) and ellipsis (…)
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students to discuss the use of punctuation marks: colon (:), semicolon (;), apostrophe (‘) and ellipsis (…) in writing
Dictation: Read a text to students in intervals so that they write while observing punctuation marks: colon (:), semicolon (;), apostrophe (‘) and ellipsis (…)
activities.assessment_criteria: A passage has been written correctly observing the punctuation marks colon (:), semicolon (;), apostrophe (‘) and ellipsis (…)

activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Using writing in communication according to various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (b) Using appropriate vocabulary in essay writing according to the topic
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students to discuss and write the main idea of each paragraph, then complete the essay using appropriate vocabulary
activities.assessment_criteria: Appropriate vocabulary has been used well in essay writing according to the topic

activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Using writing in communication according to various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (c) Writing an official letter observing the correct structure
suggested_methods: Role play: Assign students roles in groups according to the parts of an official letter, then guide them to role play
Questions and Answers: Guide students to write official letters observing their parts
activities.assessment_criteria: An official letter has been written correctly observing its structure

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of what is listened to or read
activities.learning_activity: (a) Narrating a story listened to correctly
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students to discuss basic matters when narrating a story
Narration: Guide students to narrate their lives during the holiday
activities.assessment_criteria: The story listened to has been narrated correctly

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of what is listened to or read
activities.learning_activity: (b) Interpreting the main message contained in the story and real-life environments
suggested_methods: Questions and answers: Guide students to explain the lessons they get from the story by asking them questions

Fishbowl: Guide students to sit in two circles (inner circle and outer circle), then those in the inner circle explain the lessons they get from the story and those in the outer circle add what is missing
activities.assessment_criteria: The main message contained in the story has been interpreted correctly considering real-life environments

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of what is listened to or read
activities.learning_activity: (c) Relating the behavior of characters in the story to real-life environments
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students in groups to discuss how the behavior of characters resembles real-life environments
Observation: Give students the profile of each character, then guide them to investigate by comparing with people in their community
activities.assessment_criteria: The behavior of characters in the story has been correctly related to real-life environments

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of what is listened to or read
activities.learning_activity: (d) Clarifying the meaning of idioms and proverbs contained in the story correctly
suggested_methods: Game: Prepare two large cards, write the word “idiom” on one and the word “proverb” on the other, then write many idioms and proverbs on separate papers, and guide students holding cards written idiom to stand in front of the large card written ‘idiom’ while raising them, and those holding cards written proverb should do the same
Game: Form two teams, then one team should mention an idiom and the second team should say its meaning. Also, do the same for proverbs by exchanging roles
activities.assessment_criteria: The meaning of idioms and proverbs contained in the story has been clarified correctly

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of what is listened to or read
activities.specific_competence: 2.2 Reading texts fluently and with comprehension
activities.learning_activity: (a) Reading long simple texts
suggested_methods: Questions and answers: Guide students to read long simple texts, then ask students questions about those texts
Project work: Guide students to visit the library to read long simple texts, then identify the ideas contained in those texts and present them in class
activities.assessment_criteria: Long simple texts have been read with comprehension
suggested_resources: Long simple creative and non-creative texts

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of what is listened to or read
activities.specific_competence: 2.2 Reading texts fluently and with comprehension
activities.learning_activity: (b) Presenting main ideas read in long texts
suggested_methods: Questions and answers: Guide students to read texts, then explain the main ideas they have learned
Discussion: Guide students to discuss the main ideas in the long text they have read
activities.assessment_criteria: Ideas read in long texts have been presented correctly

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Presenting arguments through speech in various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (a) Presenting arguments using vocabulary appropriate to the specific context of conversation
suggested_methods: Role play: Guide students to role play presenting arguments in a student government meeting
Inviting a guest speaker: Invite a Community Development Officer to present a topic on health or proper gender relations, then guide students to contribute arguments based on the presented topic
activities.assessment_criteria: Arguments have been presented correctly using vocabulary appropriate to the specific context of conversation

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and writing according to context
activities.learning_activity: (a) Writing a short essay observing the components of an essay
suggested_methods: Concept map: Guide students to name and explain the components of an essay starting with the first circle containing the word essay, then let them continue
Demonstration: Show a sample essay, then guide students to compose an essay observing that example
activities.assessment_criteria: A short essay has been written observing essay components

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and writing according to context
activities.learning_activity: (b) Replying to a friendly letter
suggested_methods: Questions and Answers: Guide students to reply to a friendly letter
activities.assessment_criteria: A friendly letter has been replied to correctly

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.3 Analyzing ideas presented in various texts
activities.learning_activity: (a) Analyzing various ideas that emerged in the short simple text read
suggested_methods: Project work: Guide students to visit the library to read texts, then analyze the ideas contained in the texts they have read
activities.assessment_criteria: Various ideas that emerged in the short simple text read have been analyzed fluently

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.3 Analyzing ideas presented in various texts
activities.learning_activity: (b) Explaining ideas that emerged in the short simple text through speech
suggested_methods: Reading texts: Prepare texts, divide them into groups, then guide students to read, discuss and explain the ideas emerging in those texts
activities.assessment_criteria: Ideas that emerged in the short simple text have been explained correctly through speech

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.3 Analyzing ideas presented in various texts
activities.learning_activity: (c) Summarizing information read in the short simple text through writing
suggested_methods: Questions and answers: Guide students using questions to identify main ideas in the short simple texts they have read and summarize them
activities.assessment_criteria: Information read in the short simple text has been summarized correctly through writing

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.4 Demonstrating early creative skills in various Kiswahili works
activities.learning_activity: (a) Composing simple and short plays observing rules
suggested_methods: Observation: Guide students to watch a play on television or radio and observe how characters take on roles in acting, then compose simple plays following the rules
Game: Guide students to perform the play they have composed
activities.assessment_criteria: Simple and short plays have been composed correctly observing rules

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.4 Demonstrating early creative skills in various Kiswahili works
activities.learning_activity: (b) Acting simple dramas
suggested_methods: Observation: Guide students to watch dramas on television or listen on the radio, then observe stylistic techniques and present them in class
Game: Guide students to act simple plays
activities.assessment_criteria: Simple dramas have been acted effectively

activities.learning_activity: (a) Using vocabulary in various discussions with confidence
suggested_methods: Debate: Guide students to use appropriate vocabulary in a debate
activities.assessment_criteria: Vocabulary has been used in various discussions with confidence

activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Using writing in communication according to various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (a) Identifying writing errors in texts
suggested_methods: Observation: Guide students to read texts carefully and identify writing errors
activities.assessment_criteria: Writing errors in texts have been identified
suggested_resources: Messages of greetings, speeches, computers, tablets and various texts

activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Using writing in communication according to various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (b) Correcting writing errors in texts
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students to discuss and correct errors by writing the correct one where there is a writing error
activities.assessment_criteria: Writing errors in texts have been corrected

activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Using writing in communication according to various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (c) Writing messages of greetings and speeches by observing structure and context
suggested_methods: Reading texts: Guide students to read various messages of greetings and speeches, then discuss the structure of speeches and messages of greetings

Boasting: Guide students in two teams to boast about messages of greetings and speeches by identifying their characteristics, structure, use and participants. Let one team be called messages of greetings and the second team be called speeches
Discussion: Guide students to discuss in groups things to consider when writing messages of greetings and speeches, then write messages of greetings and speeches
activities.assessment_criteria: Messages of greetings and speeches have been written by observing structure and context correctly

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of a matter listened to or read
activities.learning_activity: (a) Listening to various news items and taking notes of main ideas
suggested_methods: Narrative: Guide students to listen to news you have prepared, then write the main ideas contained in those news items
Observation: Guide students to listen to a news bulletin on the radio/television/computer, then write the main ideas they got
activities.assessment_criteria: Various news items have been listened to and main ideas have been accurately noted

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Showing understanding of a matter listened to or read
activities.learning_activity: (b) Summarizing news listened to by focusing on main ideas
suggested_methods: Questions and answers: Guide students to identify and write the main idea for each paragraph in the news they listened to, then connect the ideas to get a summary
activities.assessment_criteria: News listened to has been summarized by focusing on main ideas

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and in writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Presenting arguments through speech in various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (a) Using appropriate vocabulary in opposing or defending an argument by giving strong examples according to context
suggested_methods: Debate: Guide students by giving them a debate topic, one side to oppose and the other to defend the argument with strong examples according to context
activities.assessment_criteria: Appropriate vocabulary has been used fluently in opposing or defending an argument by giving strong examples according to context
suggested_resources: Dictionary, television, CDs, radio and voice recorder

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and in writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Presenting arguments through speech in various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (b) Using appealing language in presenting arguments
suggested_methods: Presentation: Guide students to present arguments using appealing language, that is, containing figures of speech, idioms, proverbs and sayings
activities.assessment_criteria: Appealing language has been used correctly in presenting arguments

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and in writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Presenting arguments through speech in various contexts
activities.learning_activity: (c) Giving speeches using fluent language in school contexts
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students to discuss basic things to consider when giving a speech
Role play: Guide students to role play how to give a speech showing their priorities during school leadership position campaigns
activities.assessment_criteria: Giving a speech using fluent language in a school context has been done

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and in writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.2 Analysing ideas presented in various texts
activities.learning_activity: (a) Reading various poems and dialogue poems (ngonjera)
suggested_methods: Reading texts: Guide students to read texts containing poems and dialogue poems
Observation: Guide students to listen to recorded poems and dialogue poems, then observe how they are recited and chanted
Questions and answers: Guide students to identify things to consider when chanting a poem and reciting a dialogue poem
activities.assessment_criteria: Various poems and dialogue poems have been read fluently

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and in writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.2 Analysing ideas presented in various texts
activities.learning_activity: (b) Analysing ideas arising in dialogue poems and poems read
suggested_methods: Project work: Guide students to visit the library to read dialogue poems and poems, then analyse the message contained
Discussion: Guide students to elaborate ideas that emerged in dialogue poems and poems
activities.assessment_criteria: Ideas arising in dialogue poems and poems read have been analysed correctly

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and in writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.2 Analysing ideas presented in various texts
activities.learning_activity: (c) Narrating ideas contained in dialogue poems and poems read
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students to recite dialogue poems and chant poems, then discuss the message contained
Questions and answers: Guide students to elaborate ideas that emerged in dialogue poems and poems by asking them questions
activities.assessment_criteria: Ideas contained in dialogue poems and poems read have been narrated fluently

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and in writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.3 Demonstrating early skills of creativity in various Kiswahili works
activities.learning_activity: (a) Composing a poem and a dialogue poem
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students to discuss and write words with similar endings, then write words with four syllables, then add other words with four syllables (totaling eight syllables), then compose dialogue poems and poems using those words
activities.assessment_criteria: Dialogue poems and poems have been composed correctly
suggested_resources: Dialogue poems, poems and real objects

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Presenting arguments through speech and in writing according to context
activities.specific_competence: 3.3 Demonstrating early skills of creativity in various Kiswahili works
activities.learning_activity: (b) Reciting dialogue poems and chanting poems
suggested_methods: Observation: Guide students to watch dialogue poems and poems on television and radio and observe stylistic techniques used
Game: Guide students to recite dialogue poems and chant poems
activities.assessment_criteria: Dialogue poems have been recited and poems have been chanted correctly

translation_note: English rendering of the Kiswahili TIE syllabus, for English-medium schools. Not TIE's own wording — see translation_of for the verbatim source.
